_note: Demo-mode explanations for POC4. Each entry was generated by Claude (Anthropic), reading only the structured evidence pack that explain.py builds for that scenario — the exact numbers below and nowhere else. explain.py uses these when no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in the environment; point it at a live key and it calls the real Anthropic API with the same evidence pack instead of reading this file. Nothing here influences which situations fire or how they're ranked — that stays 100% deterministic, upstream in detect_and_correlate.py.

knu_skool_west_coast.narrative: Search interest and sales for the Knu Skool have both climbed steadily on the West Coast for ten straight weeks, while Vans' own warehouse stock has fallen by over a third. PacSun's San Diego store is the tightest link in that chain — its shelf stock has dropped 69% to just 28 units, right as demand is accelerating.
key_evidence: Searches up 30% and sales up 22% over the 10-week window
Vans-side inventory down 35%, from about 1,800 to 1,170 units
PacSun - San Diego down to 28 units on hand, a 69% drop
knu_skool_west_coast.confidence_rationale: 96% because all three signals moved in the same direction nearly every week, not just once or twice, and the size of each move (30% / 22% / -35%) is well past the 15% threshold the rule treats as a real trend.
knu_skool_west_coast.suggested_talking_point: Call PacSun - San Diego this week — demand is outrunning supply and they're the dealer most exposed.

old_skool_west_coast.narrative: Shoppers are searching for the Old Skool on the West Coast more than ever — up 35% over ten weeks — but the share of those visits turning into a sale has nearly halved. The interest is there; something between the search and the checkout is losing people.
key_evidence: Conversion rate down 45%, roughly cut in half
Sales stayed close to flat, so inventory isn't the constraint here
old_skool_west_coast.confidence_rationale: 92% — both the rise in search and the drop in conversion held consistently week over week, and the size of the conversion decline is large enough that it's very unlikely to be noise.
old_skool_west_coast.suggested_talking_point: Get UX or pricing to look at the Old Skool product page and checkout flow — traffic isn't the problem, something after the click is.

sk8hi_midwest.narrative: Sk8-Hi sales in the Midwest are still climbing, but returns have nearly doubled over the same ten weeks and reviews have swung sharply negative. That combination usually means a quality or fit issue is surfacing just as more people are buying it.
key_evidence: Sales up 18%, so this isn't a demand problem
Returns up 88%, from 8 to 15 a week
Review sentiment fell 0.62 points, crossing into negative territory
sk8hi_midwest.confidence_rationale: 90% — returns and sentiment both moved sharply and consistently in the same direction, well past the threshold for a real signal rather than a bad week or two.
sk8hi_midwest.suggested_talking_point: Loop in quality/merchandising before the next replenishment order — something about this batch or fit is turning buyers into returners.

old_skool_northeast.narrative: The same Opportunity pattern is showing up for the Old Skool in the Northeast, just at a smaller scale — search and sales are both up around a fifth, inventory is down, and Journeys' Boston store is running low. It's a real signal, just not as sharp as the West Coast case.
key_evidence: Journeys - Boston down to 46 units, a 39% drop
old_skool_northeast.confidence_rationale: 82% — the direction is consistent across the window, but the moves are smaller in magnitude than the West Coast Knu Skool case, which is exactly why it ranks lower even though it's the same situation type.
old_skool_northeast.suggested_talking_point: Worth a heads-up to Journeys - Boston, though it's a lower priority than the West Coast Knu Skool situation.

knu_skool_northeast.narrative: Knu Skool sales in the Northeast are up, but so are returns — up nearly 78% — and reviews have cooled noticeably, though not as sharply as the Midwest Sk8-Hi case. Worth a look, but a smaller fire than that one.
key_evidence: Sentiment down 0.39 points, a milder dip than the Midwest case's -0.62
knu_skool_northeast.confidence_rationale: 80% — returns and sentiment both cleared the threshold, but the sentiment swing was gentler, which is why this ranks just behind the Midwest Product Problem.
knu_skool_northeast.suggested_talking_point: Add this to the quality review queue behind the Sk8-Hi Midwest issue — same pattern, smaller so far.

sk8hi_west_coast.narrative: On the numbers alone, this looks like one of the strongest Opportunities in the whole set — search up 29%, sales up 21%, inventory down 34%. But 80% of this window ran on a promotion, so a good chunk of that lift is very likely the discount talking, not organic demand. That's why the confidence was cut from 95 to 71 and it fell out of the top 5.
key_evidence: Raw signal strength (95) would rank #1 or #2 on its own
80% of the 10-week window had an active promo running
Confidence discounted 25% to 71, dropping it below the Northeast Product Problem case
sk8hi_west_coast.confidence_rationale: Discounted specifically because of the promo overlap — the rule doesn't know how much of the lift is the discount versus real demand, so it lowers confidence rather than guessing.
sk8hi_west_coast.suggested_talking_point: Don't reallocate stock off this one yet — pull a non-promo week's numbers first to see if the demand holds without the discount.
